answer.rationale: p99 latency on the write path is 5x target and climbing, with a release that went out 2 hours ago and settlement traffic at peak. Inherited memory_b1 records that a rollback cleared a prior checkout error spike with no customer impact, and memory_b6 records that staged canary gating has reliably caught bad builds within an hour — both support the pattern that a recent release is the likely cause of a write-path regression and that a rollback is the safest fast intervention. With only one action available, rollback preserves customer writes, avoids the cost of a regional failover during peak settlement, and leaves capacity or circuit-breaker options available if latency does not recover after the rollback completes.
